topic.name: HTMX & Server-Driven UI
topic.tagline: Hypermedia, partial swaps, and progressive enhancement without a SPA.
topic.description: HTMX lets the server return HTML fragments that update the page directly. Learn the request/response contract, hx-target and swap modes, CSRF, validation errors, out-of-band updates, history, caching, and the cases where a dedicated client framework is still the better tool.

questions.prompt: What does an HTMX endpoint usually return to the browser?
choices: A JSON payload that a client-side renderer turns into HTML
An HTML fragment that HTMX swaps into the page
A compiled JavaScript bundle
A WebSocket frame
questions.explanation: HTMX is hypermedia-oriented: the server returns HTML, often just a fragment, and HTMX inserts it at the target. JSON is still possible, but it is not the default contract.

questions.prompt: Which attribute decides where the response is inserted?
choices: hx-get
hx-target
hx-swap
hx-trigger
questions.explanation: hx-target selects the element to update. hx-swap controls how it is replaced: innerHTML, outerHTML, beforeend, and so on.

questions.prompt: What happens when a button with hx-post="/items/" is clicked?
choices: The browser performs a normal form submission and reloads the page.
HTMX sends a background POST request and swaps the response into the target.
HTMX opens a WebSocket connection to /items/.
The button toggles a CSS class without a request.
questions.explanation: hx-post issues an AJAX POST when the element is triggered. The response is inserted according to hx-target and hx-swap; the page does not reload unless the server sends HX-Redirect or the code forces it.

questions.prompt: What does progressive enhancement mean in an HTMX app?
choices: The app requires JavaScript before any content can be read.
Links and forms work as normal HTTP requests, and HTMX upgrades them when JavaScript is available.
Every response must include a fallback JSON API.
The server renders only the first request and the client takes over afterwards.
questions.explanation: The HTML should remain usable without JavaScript. HTMX intercepts normal links and forms and turns them into partial updates, but the same URLs still need to work as full-page requests.

questions.prompt: Which response header tells HTMX to perform a full browser redirect?
choices: HX-Push-Url
HX-Redirect
HX-Refresh
HX-Location
questions.explanation: HX-Redirect sets window.location for a full navigation. HX-Location performs a client-side-style redirect without a full page reload, and HX-Push-Url only changes the address bar.

choices: The first .card in the document
The nearest ancestor of the triggering element that matches .card
The element with id card
The next sibling with class .card
questions.explanation: closest walks up from the triggered element. It is useful when a button inside a card should update that card rather than a global container.

questions.prompt: How does hx-swap="outerHTML" differ from the default innerHTML?
choices: It replaces the target element itself with the response.
It inserts the response after the target.
It replaces only the target's text content.
It disables swapping for that request.
questions.explanation: innerHTML replaces the target's children. outerHTML replaces the target element, so the response must include the wrapper element again if you want to keep it.

questions.prompt: What is the safest way to send Django's CSRF token with an HTMX POST?
choices: Mark the view with @csrf_exempt.
Include {% csrf_token %} in the form, or send the token in the X-CSRFToken header.
Disable CsrfViewMiddleware for AJAX requests.
Use GET instead of POST.
questions.explanation: Django accepts the token in the csrfmiddlewaretoken form field or the X-CSRFToken header. Keep CSRF protection on; csrf_exempt is not an AJAX solution.

questions.prompt: By default, what does HTMX do with a 422 response?
choices: It swaps the response into the target like a 200.
It does not swap; it fires an error event, unless you configure beforeSwap to allow it.
It retries the request three times.
It reloads the whole page.
questions.explanation: HTMX swaps 2xx responses by default. For a validation response with status 422, either return 200 with the re-rendered form or handle htmx:beforeSwap and set shouldSwap = true.

questions.prompt: What does hx-trigger="keyup changed delay:300ms" do?
choices: Fires on every keypress and sends every request immediately.
Fires after keyup only when the value changed, waiting 300 ms to debounce.
Fires once when the page loads.
Fires on Enter only.
questions.explanation: changed suppresses requests when the value did not change, and delay:300ms debounces rapid typing. This is the usual pattern for live search.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of hx-swap-oob in a response?
choices: To update a different element on the page from the same response.
To bypass CSRF checks.
To stream a response over WebSockets.
To keep the response out of the browser history.
questions.explanation: Out-of-band swaps let one response update several regions: for example, append a row to a list and replace a counter or toast. The OOB element is matched by id or a selector in the attribute.

questions.prompt: What does the HX-Trigger response header do?
choices: It triggers a custom client-side event that other scripts can listen for.
It tells Django to run a management command.
It forces a full page reload.
It changes the HTTP method of the next request.
questions.explanation: HX-Trigger dispatches an event on the triggering element or body, optionally with JSON detail. It is useful for closing a dialog, refreshing a counter, or showing a toast without coupling the server to DOM details.

questions.prompt: Why must a URL used with hx-push-url="true" also work as a normal page?
choices: Because HTMX always reloads the page afterwards.
Because users can refresh, bookmark, or open the URL directly, so the server must render a complete page.
Because hx-push-url disables fragment responses.
Because the browser blocks history changes on partial responses.
questions.explanation: Pushing a URL only changes the address bar. On refresh or direct navigation there is no HTMX request context, so the same view must return a full page. This is progressive enhancement applied to history.

questions.prompt: What problem does hx-sync="closest form:abort" solve?
choices: It prevents stale responses from an earlier keystroke overwriting a newer result by coordinating requests.
It encrypts form data in transit.
It resets the form after every request.
It disables the form while the page loads.
questions.explanation: When several requests can be in flight, hx-sync controls which one wins. abort cancels the previous request for the same form; drop ignores new requests while one is active. Without coordination, a slow response can overwrite a newer one.

questions.prompt: When is HTMX a poor fit?
choices: A CRUD form that benefits from server-rendered validation errors
A page with complex local state, offline editing, or a canvas/rich-text editor
A list with filters and pagination
A dashboard that updates one widget at a time
questions.explanation: HTMX shines when the server owns state and HTML is the contract. Highly interactive client-side tools, offline-first collaboration, and rich editors usually need a dedicated client framework or a hybrid island.

flashcards.front: How does HTMX differ from a JSON SPA?
flashcards.back: The server returns HTML fragments, not JSON that the client must render. State and navigation stay closer to the server; HTMX swaps fragments into the DOM. A SPA is better when complex client-side state must live in the browser.

flashcards.front: What do hx-target and hx-swap control?
flashcards.back: hx-target chooses the element to update. hx-swap chooses how: innerHTML (default), outerHTML, beforeend, afterend, delete, and so on. Use CSS selectors plus closest/find/next for local targets.

flashcards.front: How do you send Django's CSRF token with HTMX?
flashcards.back: Either include {% csrf_token %} inside the form that hx-post submits, or send the token in the X-CSRFToken header via hx-headers. Do not disable CSRF middleware or exempt the view.

flashcards.front: How should an HTMX form return validation errors?
flashcards.back: Re-render the form fragment with bound errors so the user keeps their input. Return 200, or return 422 and configure htmx:beforeSwap to allow the swap. Do not return a JSON error page for an HTML target.

A response can update more than its main target. An element with hx-swap-oob="true" (or a selector such as beforeend:#toasts) is matched elsewhere in the page. Use it for counters, toasts, and secondary panels; keep ids unique.

flashcards.front: What are HX-Trigger and HX-Redirect used for?
flashcards.back: HX-Trigger fires a client-side custom event, optionally with JSON detail, so other scripts can react. HX-Redirect performs a full browser redirect. HX-Location changes location without a full reload; HX-Push-Url only updates history.

flashcards.front: How do you prevent stale HTMX responses?
flashcards.back: Use hx-sync to coordinate requests: closest form:abort cancels the previous request, while drop ignores new ones. Debounce inputs with changed delay:300ms. Test slow responses, not just fast local ones.
flashcards.front_code:
<input hx-get="/search/" hx-trigger="keyup changed delay:300ms"
       hx-target="#results" hx-sync="this:abort">
